name: Slovenia
tagline: Free tuition for EU students, but very few English bachelor's
summary: Slovenia is cheap, safe, extremely good-looking, and free: as an EU citizen you pay no tuition for full-time bachelor study, exactly like a Slovenian. The catch is blunt - almost all bachelor teaching is in Slovene. Across the four public universities there are only around sixteen English-taught bachelor programmes in total, and the University of Ljubljana has just one. If one of those programmes happens to be what you want, Slovenia is one of the best-value places in Europe. If not, it is not an option.
whyConsider: Full-time bachelor tuition is free for EU/EEA citizens - the same deal Slovenian students get
Living costs are genuinely low: a student dorm room is EUR 120-250 a month and a student meal costs you about EUR 4.37
One central application portal, eVS, handles everything including the recognition of your IB Diploma
University of Primorska in Koper has the widest English-taught choice, including mathematics, computer science and bioinformatics
Ljubljana is small, walkable and an hour from both the Alps and the Adriatic
watchOuts: English-taught bachelor's are very thin: roughly 1 at Ljubljana, 5 at Maribor, 9 at Primorska, 1 at Nova Gorica
Private international students are generally not eligible for university dormitories except in Maribor - dorms are reserved for exchange and scholarship students
No page found gives IB-specific minimum points or a mapping onto the Slovenian Matura; you must ask the ENIC-NARIC Centre or the faculty directly
Recognition of your foreign qualification is compulsory and is done by the university itself, with cost and processing time not published
Some published non-EU fee figures are old (Primorska's range is labelled 2021/2022), so treat fee pages with suspicion

notes: The IB is accepted as an admission qualification, but only through a formal recognition procedure ('priznavanje'). The national portal states a candidate who completed schooling abroad 'is obliged to acquire a decision on the recognition of the foreign education, if they have not obtained one already'.

The higher education institutions themselves are the competent bodies for the recognition procedure. The Slovenian ENIC-NARIC Centre, inside the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation, is the national information point (enic-naric@gov.si, +386 1 478 46 00).
The recognition application is submitted together with the study application through the eVS portal.

No page read on 2026-09-22 published IB-specific minimum points, an HL/SL mapping onto the Slovenian Matura, or a grade conversion table. Contact the ENIC-NARIC Centre and the specific faculty before you rely on anything here.

For domestic applicants the access requirement is the Matura, a final examination taken before 1 June 1995, or a vocational Matura plus an additional general Matura subject. How an IB Diploma is scored against this for selective programmes is not documented publicly.

steps: Wait for the call for enrolment (razpis za vpis) for your year, published by February at the latest. It sets the deadlines and the number of places per programme.
Create a SI-PASS login and open an application in the eVS portal.
Enter your personal and residence details, then your secondary education - this is where you also trigger the recognition procedure for your IB Diploma.
Choose your programme or programmes. EU citizens apply for the places intended for Slovenian citizens; non-EU citizens apply through the separate quota for foreigners.
Upload your supporting documents. Scans and photographs are accepted.
Submit, then follow the individual institution's enrolment process once you are selected.
application.selectionNotes: Programmes with more applicants than places apply 'omejitev vpisa' - an enrolment limitation - and rank applicants on points. The exact points formula, and how IB grades are converted into it, was not found on any page read on 2026-09-22; it is set out in each faculty's razpis for the relevant year. No separate application fee for eVS was found.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Very limited. Around 16 English-taught bachelor programmes across the four public universities: University of Ljubljana 1 (Business and Economics); University of Maribor 5 (Contemporary Tourism Practices; Economic and business sciences; Business administration; Economic and Technical Logistics; System logistics); University of Primorska 9 (Tourism; Tourism destination management; Anthropology; Cultural Heritage; Academic Bachelor in Management; Bioinformatics; Computer Science; Mathematics; Mathematics and Computer Science; plus Wood Innovation for Sustainability); University of Nova Gorica 1 (Physics and Astrophysics). Private colleges add a further handful.
notes: Slovene is not required for the specific English-taught programmes listed, but it is required for the overwhelming majority of bachelor teaching in the country.
No page read on 2026-09-22 stated whether IB English A or B is accepted as proof of English, or gave IELTS/TOEFL thresholds. Check with each faculty for the programme you want.
The programme list above comes from the national Study in Slovenia portal rather than from each faculty, so confirm the programme still runs in English before applying.

tuitionEuEea.value: Free. The University of Ljubljana states there are 'No tuition fees for full-time bachelor's and master's studies' for Slovenian citizens and 'students from EU countries, Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway'. University of Primorska confirms 'full-time study at the 1st and 2nd level of study is free from tuition fee'. University of Nova Gorica lists EUR 0.00 per year for full-time EU/Slovenian citizens. Part-time study is not free, even for EU citizens.
tuitionEuEea.year: 2025/2026 (Nova Gorica, stated explicitly); Ljubljana and Primorska pages undated

tuitionNonEu.value: Roughly EUR 2,000-11,000 a year for bachelor study depending on the programme, per the national portal. University of Primorska publishes EUR 2,400-3,750 a year, but that range is explicitly labelled 2021/2022 and is probably out of date. University of Nova Gorica publishes EUR 2,800-3,500 a year for 2025/2026, though its wording attaches that bracket to part-time study. University of Ljubljana publishes only faculty-specific PDF price lists. Treat all of these as indicative.
tuitionNonEu.year: National range undated; Primorska 2021/2022; Nova Gorica 2025/2026

costs.applicationFee: No application fee for eVS was found. University of Primorska charges a registration fee of approximately EUR 50 a year.

livingCostMonthly.value: Roughly EUR 400-650 a month. Student dormitory EUR 120-250; a double room in a private flat EUR 150-200; a single room EUR 200-350. Subsidised student meals: the state contributes EUR 2.63 and you pay up to EUR 4.37. Public transport: EUR 1.50 for a 90-minute ticket, EUR 25 for a monthly student pass.
livingCostMonthly.year: Undated on the page read on 2026-09-22

notes: The subsidised student meal scheme ('studentski boni') is a real, significant saving and is one of the things that makes Slovenia cheap to live in.
The free-tuition rule applies to full-time study only. If you end up studying part-time you will pay, EU citizen or not.

funding: Ad futura international mobility scholarships, administered nationally.
A Public Call for Scholarships for Foreign Citizens exists but is aimed at Western Balkan postgraduate students, so it is unlikely to help a Danish IB applicant.
No general merit scholarship aimed at EU bachelor applicants was found - the funding story in Slovenia is that tuition is free, not that scholarships are plentiful.
Danish SU for a full degree abroad requires programme approval by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen; check with your studievejleder.
workRights: Slovenia has an unusual system called studentsko delo - student work through official Student Services, using a referral document ('napotnica'). Minimum referenced pay is EUR 7.21 an hour, with a 15.5% pension and disability deduction for all students, leaving about EUR 6.20. Foreign students additionally have 22.5% withheld as income tax prepayment, reclaimable if your home country has a double taxation treaty with Slovenia. Weekly or monthly hour limits, and any EU/non-EU eligibility difference, were not stated on the page read on 2026-09-22.
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you must get a residence registration certificate within your first three months, applied for at the local administrative unit. You need a signed application, a biometric photo, a valid passport or ID, proof of address, proof of admission, proof of financial means of at least EUR 494.09 a month, and health insurance (EHIC). Fees are EUR 9.10 registration, EUR 4.50 application and EUR 12.32 for card printing, and renewal is typically by 30 September each year. Non-EU students must obtain a temporary residence permit before entering Slovenia, through a Slovenian diplomatic mission, and should get a police clearance certificate before travelling.
housing: This is the practical catch. Study in Slovenia states plainly that 'If you are coming as a private international student, unfortunately you do not have the option of staying in university student dormitories, except in Maribor' - the dorms are mainly reserved for exchange and scholarship students. In Ljubljana, dorm places where available are first-come-first-served at EUR 80-160 a month for a double room. Maribor opens applications after acceptance and emails information in July for the first semester; cost EUR 540-850 a semester. Primorska (around EUR 190 a month shared) and Nova Gorica (EUR 120-170 a month) send accommodation information about a month before the semester starts. Budget for the private market.
healthcare: As a Danish EU citizen you are covered for necessary care with an EHIC. Students without EU/EEA or bilateral-agreement cover must buy compulsory Slovenian health insurance at EUR 126.33 a month (8.2% of average gross earnings), and the national portal recommends supplementary private insurance on top because the compulsory cover is only partial.

institutions.name: University of Ljubljana
institutions.englishBachelors: One confirmed: Business and Economics, at the School of Economics and Business
institutions.note: By far the largest and oldest Slovenian university, but with essentially one English-taught bachelor programme - worth applying to only if that programme is what you want.

institutions.name: University of Maribor
institutions.englishBachelors: Five confirmed: Contemporary Tourism Practices; Economic and business sciences; Business administration; Economic and Technical Logistics; System logistics
institutions.note: Calls itself the most international university in Slovenia, and it is the only one where private international students can get a dormitory place.

institutions.name: University of Primorska
institutions.englishBachelors: Nine or ten - the widest choice in Slovenia: Tourism; Tourism destination management; Anthropology; Cultural Heritage; Academic Bachelor in Management; Bioinformatics; Computer Science; Mathematics; Mathematics and Computer Science; Wood Innovation for Sustainability
institutions.note: On the Adriatic coast and the one Slovenian university with a real English-taught bachelor offering, especially in maths and computing through its FAMNIT faculty.

institutions.name: University of Nova Gorica
institutions.note: Tiny and research-intensive, on the Italian border, with an unusual School for Viticulture and Enology.

institutions.name: Alma Mater Europaea
institutions.englishBachelors: Eight identified: Archives Management; Physiotherapy; Humanities; Business Management; Dance/Choreography; Social Gerontology; Web and Information Technologies; Nursing
institutions.note: Private, and paradoxically the institution with the most English-taught bachelor programmes in the country - but private means you pay, so check the fee.

institutions.name: GEA College
institutions.englishBachelors: Entrepreneurship confirmed on the national English-programmes list; other programmes advertised but not cross-confirmed
institutions.note: A small private business school with a large network of partner institutions; describes itself as boutique.

institutions.name: International School for Social and Business Studies
institutions.englishBachelors: Two identified: Economy in Contemporary Society; Business in Contemporary Society
institutions.note: Small private business faculty in Celje with Erasmus+ links; the website URL could not be confirmed directly, so check it before relying on it.

institutions.name: DOBA Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: None identified - the bachelor programmes listed are in Slovene
institutions.note: Describes itself as the first private educational institution in Slovenia and specialises in online and distance learning.

institutions.name: Faculty of Information Studies Novo Mesto
institutions.englishBachelors: None identified - all listed programmes are in Slovene
institutions.note: A small specialised informatics faculty with an unusual video game development programme, but taught in Slovene.

institutions.name: Academy of Fine Arts and Design, University of Ljubljana
institutions.englishBachelors: Not confirmed; ALUO did not appear on the national list of English-taught bachelor programmes
institutions.note: Slovenia's main public art academy. Do not confuse it with the separate private Academy of Visual Arts (AVA), which does list English-taught bachelor programmes.

institutions.name: Academy of Music, University of Ljubljana
institutions.englishBachelors: Not confirmed; did not appear on the national list of English-taught bachelor programmes
institutions.note: Slovenia's main public music academy; entry is by audition and you should assume Slovene at bachelor level.

institutions.name: IEDC-Bled School of Management
institutions.englishBachelors: None - IEDC offers no bachelor degrees at all
institutions.note: Internationally respected but entirely executive and postgraduate - listed here so you know not to apply to it as a school leaver.
